diagnosis_summary: Public Rock 19.2 source used a shared mutable Dictionary cache in the singleton AzureBlobStorageClient and performed an unsynchronized ContainsKey/Add sequence. A Rock maintainer added concurrent regression tests, confirmed that they reproduced the reported race, replaced the cache with ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd, and closed the issue. Develop commit d66a4f492306b10c7bd71aa13d54273918c941a3 contains the original fix; commit c2f5bb4bf37139dbfa24e01de1378cdbbe2f4ff2 carries it in the hotfix-19.4 ancestry, matching the current Fixed in v19.4 label.
workaround_summaries: Use a Rock build proven to contain hotfix commit c2f5bb4bf37139dbfa24e01de1378cdbbe2f4ff2, develop commit d66a4f492306b10c7bd71aa13d54273918c941a3, or an independently verified equivalent. Until upgraded, an application-pool recycle may restore service after the reported failure, but it does not remove the concurrency defect and is not a durable fix.

verification_playbook.goal: Determine whether the instance combines the vulnerable Azure container cache implementation with an Azure-backed binary file type.
prerequisites: Know the exact installed Rock version or build ancestry.
Have read-only access to file-storage configuration and bounded exception counts.

steps.title: Check build ancestry
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the installed package contains commit d66a4f492306b10c7bd71aa13d54273918c941a3, which replaces the shared Dictionary path with ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd.
steps.expected_if_affected: The installed build uses the earlier unsynchronized container cache implementation.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: The installed build contains the fixing commit or an independently verified equivalent implementation.

steps.title: Check whether Azure storage is in use
steps.instructions: Inspect Binary File Type storage-provider configuration without saving it. Record only whether at least one relevant type uses the Azure Blob provider; do not record account names, container names, keys, or file details.
steps.expected_if_affected: At least one active Binary File Type uses Azure Blob storage and the installed build lacks the fix.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: No Binary File Type uses Azure Blob storage, or the installed build contains the fix.
evidence_to_record: Azure provider present yes or no

steps.title: Check for the bounded exception signature
steps.instructions: Review only a bounded count of recent exceptions matching the Azure container-cache duplicate-key signature. Do not export exception bodies, request URLs, users, file names, storage identifiers, or stack traces.
steps.expected_if_affected: The vulnerable configuration is present and matching exceptions occur under concurrent file access.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: No matching exceptions are present in the bounded window, although absence does not prove the race cannot occur on a vulnerable build.

limitations: A concurrency race cannot be safely disproved by a single production observation.
Do not load-test production storage to force reproduction; the maintainer's source regression test is the authoritative reproduction.

context.scope: Azure-backed BinaryFile storage under concurrent cache population
exact source revision; release package inclusion remains independently verifiable
official fix release line; verify the exact installed package
